- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 18:21
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Title: Navigating the Future of the Multipolar World Order: Projections and Theoretical Perspectives
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Abstract: This paper seeks to explore potential scenarios for the future of the multipolar world order, drawing upon scholarly theories and historical examples to provide context and insight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The paper will explore scenarios through the lens of three key dimensions: the resurgence of great power rivalries, increased regionalization and fragmentation, and the strengthening of international institutions and norms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Theories and Projections under "The Resurgence of Great Power Rivalries" include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Realism: Emphasizes the anarchic nature of the international system and the centrality of power and security concerns.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Power Transition Theory: Global conflicts arise when a rising power challenges an existing hegemon, exemplified by the U.S.-China rivalry.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Thucydides Trap: Suggests that fear and insecurity from a rising power can lead to aggression from established powers, with examples like the U.S.-China trade war.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Theories and Projections under "Increased Regionalization and Fragmentation" include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Neofunctionalism: Increased cooperation in one area can lead to greater integration in others, as seen in regional blocs like the EU and ASEAN.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Constructivism: Emphasizes the role of norms and identity in shaping international relations, leading to regionalization based on shared factors.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Regional Security Complex Theory: Security concerns of states in a region are interconnected, leading to pronounced regional conflicts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Theories and Projections under "Strengthening International Institutions and Norms" include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Liberal Institutionalism: International institutions promote cooperation and reduce conflict among states.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Normative Power Europe: The EU can exert influence through the promotion of its values and norms.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] Global Governance: Emphasizes coordinated action among states to address transnational challenges.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Conclusion: The future of the multipolar world order remains uncertain, influenced by the resurgence of great power rivalries, regionalization, and the strengthening of institutions.
